title: There are people who know church language better than they know the voice of God.
paragraphs: There are people who know church language better than they know the voice of God.
People who can quote verses but cannot recognize conviction anymore.
People who can perform holiness publicly while secretly dying spiritually in private.
And if we are honest… this has happened to more people than most churches are willing to admit.
Some people are closer to religion than they are to God.
That sentence sounds harsh until Scripture itself exposes it.
The frightening reality of the Gospel is that the people who looked the holiest were often the furthest from the heart of God.
In Matthew 15:8, Jesus quotes the prophet Isaiah and says:
“This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me.”
Ho laos houtos tois cheilesin me tima, hē de kardia autōn porrō apechei ap’ emou.
The word kardia means “heart,” not merely emotions, but the deepest inner self — desires, will, conscience, spiritual center.
And the word porrō means distant. Far away. Removed.
Jesus was describing people who mastered outward worship while remaining inwardly detached from God Himself.
Because you can learn Christian culture without surrendering your soul.
You can sing worship songs without worship.
You can preach sermons without intimacy.
You can wear modest clothes while carrying hidden pride.
You can defend doctrine while lacking love.
You can attend church every Sunday while resisting repentance Monday through Saturday.
Religion can teach behavior modification without heart transformation.
But the Gospel was never about cosmetic holiness.
In the Hebrew Scriptures, God repeatedly warns Israel about this spiritual illusion.
Vayehi yir’atam oti mitzvat anashim melumadah.
“Their fear of Me has become a commandment taught by men.”
This is why some people panic when routines break.
Because routines were carrying a relationship they never truly developed with God.
Remove the platform, the church title, the audience, the routine, the social image… and suddenly they do not know how to stand before God alone.
But intimacy with God survives in secret places.
“When you pray, go into your room and shut the door…”
The Greek phrase tameion refers to an inner private chamber.
God has always cared more about who you are in hidden places than who you pretend to be publicly.
That is why the Pharisees struggled so much with Jesus.
They focused on ceremonial purity while plotting murder internally.
“You are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but within are full of dead people’s bones.”
Some people have mastered looking spiritually alive while emotionally, morally, and spiritually decaying internally.
And social media has amplified this problem.
But heaven is not deceived by aesthetics.
God sees beyond edited captions, staged humility, and public Christian performance.
Ki ha’adam yir’eh la’einayim, va’Adonai yir’eh lalevav.
“Man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.”
The Hebrew word levav means inner man, conscience, desires, motives.
God examines what cameras cannot capture.
And this is where the article becomes uncomfortable.
Because religion often gives people the illusion of safety while their soul slowly hardens.
You can become so familiar with Christian language that conviction no longer penetrates you.
You hear sermons but never tremble.
You read Scripture but never surrender.
You discuss theology but never repent.
Paul warned about this in 2 Timothy 3:5:
“Having the appearance of godliness, but denying its power.”
The Greek word for “appearance” is morphōsin.
Religion without God eventually becomes performance exhaustion.
That is why some people secretly feel numb in church.
And deep down they know it.
The Pharisees knew Scripture intellectually, yet missed the Messiah standing directly in front of them.
Think about how devastating that is.
The most religious people in Israel failed to recognize God incarnate.
Because pride blinds faster than ignorance.
Religion often makes people harder to correct because they confuse familiarity with faithfulness.
But Jesus did not come to create polished religious actors.
One of the most dangerous spiritual conditions is believing you are spiritually healthy because you appear morally disciplined.
The tax collector in Luke 18 understood this better than the Pharisee.
And Jesus said the sinner went home justified.
Ho theos, hilastheti moi tō hamartōlō.
“God, be merciful to me, the sinner.”
The word hilastheti carries the idea of atonement, mercy, reconciliation.
That desperate prayer mattered more to God than religious self-congratulation.
Some of the people closest to the kingdom are not the loudest religious voices.
Sometimes they are exhausted people quietly crying in their room asking God not to give up on them.
People religion overlooked but Jesus pursued.
Because Jesus is not searching for flawless performers.
He is searching for surrendered hearts.
And maybe the hardest truth is this:
But eventually every soul stands exposed before God.
“No creature is hidden from His sight.”
Panta de gymna kai tetrachēlismena tois ophthalmois autou.
And yet this is where the Gospel becomes beautiful.
Because Jesus already knew everything about us before going to the cross.

Religion says:
“Clean yourself before approaching God.”

Jesus says:
“Come to Me and I will make you new.”
The Gospel produces transformed hearts through grace.
“I will give you a new heart.”
This is why Christianity is not ultimately about rule management.
And many people sitting in churches today are exhausted because they are trying to maintain religious appearances without ever fully surrendering to Christ.
But freedom begins where honesty begins.
God cannot heal the version of you that keeps pretending.
And maybe somebody reading this knows exactly what this feels like.
You know how to look okay.
But privately you feel distant from God.
Jesus did not die for your performance.
And maybe tonight is the night you stop being merely religious… and finally become surrendered.
Some people spent years protecting an image while their soul quietly starved behind it.
